data.name: Laya
data.gender_notes: Laya is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Sanskrit, Laya means ‘dancer’ or ‘melody’. This name is derived from the root word ‘laya’ which means ‘to fold’. In Hindu mythology, Goddess Saraswati is often depicted as a dancer, representing the harmonious union of knowledge, music, and art. The name Laya is also associated with the concept of ‘laya’, the divine energy that permeates the universe and is the source of all creation.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of Divine Creativity and Knowledge
data.etymology: Laya belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Dancer, Melody.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Laya total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Laya has been popular among the Hindu community as a name for both females and males. It is believed that the name Laya carrying the blessings of Goddess Saraswati, the embodiment of knowledge, art, and music, would aid in the development of the child's artistic, creative, and intellectual abilities.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, Laya refers to the divine energy or Shakti that is present in all creation. It represents the unifying power of the universe, connecting all beings to the divine. The name Laya, derived from the root word 'laya' meaning 'to fold', is also associated with the idea of surrendering oneself to the divine will, trusting that the cosmic dance of life will unfold in perfect harmony.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Laya signifies the dissolution of the individual self in the divine consciousness. It represents the state of absorption in the Infinite, where the boundaries between the self and the Universe blur.
